text.p: - Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will try to convince International Olympic Committee authorities to hold the 2004 Olympic Games in St Petersburg by saying that Russia can find an extra $7 billion from the budget to finance the event.
- A state of emergency may be declared in Russia's north because of lack of necessary fuel.

- A new session of the State Duma lower house of Russia's parliament opens today. The peacemaking efforts of general Alexander Lebed and President Yeltsin's health are likely to be the subjects of long debates.
- Russia's Central Bank prevented a serious crisis of banking system in Moscow on Monday, September 30.
- A list of 100 top Russian polititians puts President Boris Yeltsin in third place after Prime Minister Chernomyrdin and security chief Lebed
- After failures at parliamentiary and presidential elections some polititians want just to make themselves heard, hence the possible creation of a democratic alliance.
- The social orientation of the 1997 budget, officially promised earlier, is not being observed in its draft, based on the results of the State Duma special budget group's work.
- Russian communists are anticipating a revival of their popularity as regional elections carry on.
